questions.q: In what year (approximately) did the Harappan Civilisation begin its decline?
questions.a: The decline began around 1900 BCE. A student who says "5000 years ago" or "recently" shows they are struggling to use the BCE/CE timeline correctly; they need to practice counting back from the Common Era.

questions.q: Why do historians use the word "theory" when discussing the decline of the Harappan cities?
questions.a: They use "theory" because there is no direct written record or single piece of evidence that explains exactly why the cities ended. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks history is a collection of absolute facts rather than a detective-like process of piecing together clues.

questions.q: If a river near a city changes its course, how does that impact the people living there?
questions.a: Steps: 1. Identify the river as a source of water. 2. Recognize water is needed for crops (agriculture) and daily life. 3. Conclude that if the river moves, the city loses its water supply. 4. Determine that this leads to food shortages and people moving away. A wrong answer suggests the student hasn't linked agriculture to river geography.

questions.q: Compare the impact of a dry climate on a farming village versus a large city.
questions.a: A large city relies on a massive, steady supply of grain from surrounding fields to feed thousands of people; if the climate turns dry, that supply chain breaks, causing the city to collapse. A small village might survive by moving to a new spot, but a city is fixed in place, making it more vulnerable. A wrong answer shows a lack of understanding regarding urban complexity.

questions.q: Is it possible that the Harappan Civilisation disappeared because of only one reason?
questions.a: It is unlikely, as complex societies usually fail due to a combination of factors. Historians look at multiple theories because the environment is rarely affected by only one thing. A wrong answer shows "black and white" thinking, ignoring the complexity of historical events.

questions.q: If you were an archaeologist finding a dry, ancient riverbed near a ruined city, what would you write in your report to explain the city's end?
questions.a: The report should hypothesize that the river shift caused a lack of irrigation, leading to agricultural failure and the eventual abandonment of the city by its residents. A poor answer would just say "the city died" without connecting the environmental evidence to human behavior.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The decline of the Harappan ______ refers to the period around 1900 BCE when these advanced early urban centers ceased to function as organized cities, leading to the abandonment of their complex lifestyle.
Fill in the blank: Have you ever seen a house left ______ because the well dried up or the roof collapsed?

Fill in the blank: The decline of the Harappan Civilisation refers to the period around ______ BCE when these advanced early urban centers ceased to function as organized cities, leading to the abandonment of their complex lifestyle.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to list at least two environmental theories explaining the decline and explain why historians consider these to be "theories" rather than absolute facts.
